children: Falling iron-ore prices largely reflect headwinds to steel demand in China, where construction activity remains subdued, says Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar. The property sector, which accounts for 27% of Chinese steel demand, remains the key drag, Dhar says. "While China's steel mill margins have turned slightly less negative from early October, margins remain negative enough to weigh on China's crude steel and pig iron output," he says. Seaborne iron ore supply has also tracked higher this year as the big Simandou project in Guinea ramps up. Dhar thinks these pressures are likely to persist through 2027. CBA forecasts iron ore will drop to $80/metric ton by 3Q 2027. Spot iron ore fell by 1.2% Tuesday to $87.65/ton, according to Platts, a unit of S&P Global Energy.
